title: Trump to exempt some Canadian products from tariffs amid midterm pressure
summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is poised to lift tariffs on some Canadian products as Republicans in border states lobby for relief from trade actions that have put them in a shaky political position…

image.caption: U.S. President Donald Trump will soon remove some tariffs on Canadian goods, said Maine Sen. Susan Collins on Friday. (Aaron Schwartz/Getty Images)

blocks.text: U.S. President Donald Trump is poised to lift tariffs on some Canadian products as Republicans in border states lobby for relief from trade actions that have put them in a shaky political position ahead of November's midterms.
Maine Sen. Susan Collins says some Canadian goods will soon be exempt from U.S. tariffs

Maine Republican Sen. Susan Collins said on Friday that the Trump administration will scrap tariffs on some paper and plastic products, refrigeration and packaging equipment, agricultural machinery and seaweed and algae products, among others, after she relayed how damaging these levies have been for consumers and businesses in her state.

Trump hit these products with a 50 per cent tariff in August, apparently retaliating for Canada's countermeasures on some U.S. goods that were imposed after the president first launched his trade war last year.

"I will continue working directly with administration officials to seek additional relief and encourage a broader trade agreement with Canada, our neighbour, ally and largest trading partner," Collins said in a social media statement announcing the changes.
U.S. Sen. Susan Collins campaigns in Fryeburg, Maine, earlier this month. Collins, a Republican, is in a tight race with Democrat Troy Jackson. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)

Collins, a 30-year veteran of the U.S. upper house, is in a pitched battle for re-election in Maine as she tries to hold off a Democratic challenger, Troy Jackson, who has made Trump's trade war with Canada a centrepiece of his campaign.

A moderate Republican who has sparred with Trump in the past, Collins had earlier pressured the administration to drop U.S. tariffs on products like road salt given her wintry state depends on Canadian supplies to keep the roads clear.

Another border state Republican Senate candidate, Michigan's Mike Rogers, has publicly called for an end to the trade war with Canada, saying the tariffs have raised prices at a time when inflation is already high.
Polls show Trump's trade war with Canada is deeply unpopular among American voters in both major parties.
